narrative.summary: Kiribati has no AI strategy, AI law or AI guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the Data Protection Act 2025, in force since 20 August 2026, which restricts decisions made solely by automated processing. The 2019 National ICT Policy lists AI only as a frontier technology to explore.

instruments.issuing_authority: Maneaba ni Maungatabu (House of Parliament of Kiribati); assented by the Beretitenti
instruments.current_status: Passed by the Maneaba ni Maungatabu on 18 August 2025, assented by the Beretitenti on 18 September 2025 and published by exhibition at the Maneaba on 18 September 2025 (Clerk's certificate; MICT publication page dated 18/09/2025). Section 2 leaves commencement to ministerial notice; the Notice of Commencement Date signed by the Minister for Information, Communications and Transport on 20 August 2026 and published by exhibition at the Public Office of the Beretitenti on 20 August 2026 appoints 20 August 2026 as the date the Act comes into force. The Act is administered by the Digital Transformation Office (DTO) established under the Digital Government Act 2023.
instruments.summary: Kiribati's first general data protection law, regulating the processing of personal data by public bodies and private persons, with principles on purpose limitation, minimisation and retention, data-subject rights, breach notification, data protection impact assessments for high-risk processing affecting 10,000 or more data subjects, and rules on transfers outside Kiribati. Section 17 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing of personal data that produces legal or similarly significant effects, unless the decision is necessary for a contract, authorised by a written law with safeguards, or based on consent. The Digital Transformation Office acts as the supervisory office, with investigation powers, compliance notices and administrative penalties, and the Act amends the Digital Government Act 2023, Business Names Act 2021 and Companies Act 2021.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only Kiribati law with an explicit rule on automated decision-making (s.17); governs personal-data processing in AI training and use and sets impact-assessment duties for high-risk processing.

leads.note: Official PDF on mict.gov.ki (sites/default/files/publications/National%20ICT%20Policy_3.pdf), dated 2019 on its cover. AI appears only in the Minister's foreword, a context paragraph and goal xxv 'Explore frontier technology' (promote applications of blockchain, IoT, AI incl. deep learning, big data, 5G) and an e-government bullet to 'explore' AI; no AI-specific actions, so held as a lead rather than a strategy record.
